## 4. Clocks, resets and clock-domain crossings

- Clocks: `clk`.
- Resets: `rst_n`.
- Clock and reset behaviour, and any clock-domain crossing, as described in section 6.
- Every clock domain: name, frequency, source, the logic on it. Every reset: one per domain, synchronous active low inside the domain, entering the domain only through a reset synchroniser (asynchronous assertion, synchronous release); reset sequencing between domains has a single, documented source.
- Every clock, reset and signal boundary uses a clock-domain crossing technique, listed in the file header. Never sample another domain's signal directly; never pass a multi-bit value through independent single-bit synchronisers. Example techniques:

| Technique | Use for | Library module |
|-----------|---------|----------------|
| Two- (or more) flop synchroniser (`async_reg`) | single slow level signal (enable, status, IRQ level) | `bit_sync` |
| Pulse synchroniser (toggle, sync, edge detect) | one-clock event / pulse | `pulse_sync`, `toggle_sync` |
| Reset synchroniser (async assert, sync release) | a reset entering a clock domain | `reset_sync`, `reset_ctrl` |
| Asynchronous FIFO with Gray-coded pointers | data stream at any rate ratio | `async_fifo`, `axis_async_bridge` |
| Request / acknowledge handshake (2- or 4-phase) | occasional multi-bit word, register access | `axi4_lite_cdc`, `clock_domain_bridge` |
| Multi-cycle path formulation (hold data, sync a qualifier) | multi-bit value that changes rarely | `cdc_sync_bit` + held register |
| Gray-code counter | counter value read in another domain | inside `async_fifo` |
| Glitch-free clock gate / mux | stopping or switching a clock | device BUFGCE / BUFGMUX, `clk_gen` enables |
| Related clocks from one PLL (fixed phase) | serializers, e.g. 10:1 TMDS, 7:1 LVDS | `clk_gen` outputs of one oscillator |

- Constrain every crossing (false path / max delay on the synchroniser's first flop) and document it.

## 5. Interfaces

- **s_axil_*** - AXI4-Lite slave, address [8:0], 32-bit data: interface `axil_if.slave` (`ip/shared/src/interfaces/axil_if.sv`).
- **s_axis_t*** - AXI4-Stream monitor (passive tap), tdata [23:0], tlast, tuser: interface `axis_if.monitor` (`ip/shared/src/interfaces/axis_if.sv`).

Bus ports follow the library's SystemVerilog interfaces, one definition file per type: AXI4-Stream `axis_if` (`ip/shared/src/interfaces/axis_if.sv`, modports master / slave / monitor) and AXI4-Lite `axil_if` (`ip/shared/src/interfaces/axil_if.sv`, modports master / slave). Icarus Verilog cannot drive members of interface arrays and Yosys reads interfaces only through sv2v, so keep discrete ports (<prefix>_tdata, <prefix>_awaddr, ...) and put the interface and modport in a comment line directly above each port group: `// s_axis: axis_if.slave (ip/shared/src/interfaces/axis_if.sv), DATA_W = 24`. Testbenches and Verilator flows may instantiate the interfaces directly.

| Port | Dir | Width | Group | Built when | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `clk` | input | 1 | - | - | - |
| `rst_n` | input | 1 | - | - | - |
| `feat_i` | input | [1:0] | s_axis: axis_if.monitor (ip/shared/src/interfaces/axis_if.sv), DATA_W = 24 | - | - |
| `done_o` | output | 1 | s_axis: axis_if.monitor (ip/shared/src/interfaces/axis_if.sv), DATA_W = 24 | - | - |

Back-pressure on every stream: honour tready, never drop data unless section 6 says so; valid must not depend combinationally on ready.

AXI4-Lite / register map: as listed in the behaviour text in section 6. Out-of-range accesses return SLVERR (or DECERR where stated).

## 6. Function

Implement exactly this behaviour (from the reference design's specification):

```text
Object search / measurement for target detection and
tracking. Watches an AXI4-Stream video (24-bit pixels, tuser = start of
frame, tlast = end of line) without touching it: a passive tap on the
accepted beats (tvalid & tready). Per frame it finds the pixels of the
object inside a search window and reports their bounding box; the CPU
runs the tracking loop (search the whole frame, then a window around
the predicted position) and draws the result with symbol_overlay. One
instance is one detector (one object class: its pixel test and run
widths); a design detecting several classes instantiates one per class.
  - Pixel {B, G, R} (R in [7:0]): luma Y = (R + 2 G + B) / 4, chroma
    Cb = 128 + (B - Y) / 2, Cr = 128 + (R - Y) / 2, saturation
    S = |Cb - 128| + |Cr - 128|.
  - Object pixel, inside the window (WIN_X / WIN_Y, inclusive; taken at
    the frame start) and
      CTRL.MODE = 0 (luma): Y < THRESH (CTRL.POL = 1, dark object on a
        light scene) or Y > THRESH (POL = 0);
      CTRL.MODE = 1 (colour): Y, Cb and Cr inside Y_RANGE, CB_RANGE and
        CR_RANGE (min / max inclusive) and S >= SAT_MIN (e.g. skin tone
        for faces, saturated paint for cars).
  - Run filter: a horizontal run of object pixels counts, when it ends
    (the next pixel is not an object pixel, or the end of the line), if
    it is at least MIN pixels long (RUN.MIN_W, or CTRL.MIN_RUN when
    RUN.MIN_W = 0; 0 or 1: every pixel) and, with RUN.MAX_W != 0, at
    most MAX_W long: isolated pixels, thin lines and objects wider than
    the class are ignored. The run's whole length is judged, also where
    it crosses the window's edge (a bus reaching into a car's window is
    still a bus-length run, not a car-length one); its pixels inside the
    window then add to COUNT, the sums and the box.
  - Features: feat_i carries feature_detect's bits of the beat ([0]
    edge, [1] motion). The object pixel test has two terms: term A is
    the luma / colour test above combined with the motion bit
    (CTRL.FEAT_A: the test, test OR motion, test AND motion, motion
    only), judged with RUN; term B (CTRL.TERM_B) is the edge bit, judged
    with RUN_B. Each term has its own run filter; both terms' counted
    runs add to COUNT, the box and the sums (term A's first when both
    close on the same pixel).
  - Blobs: the counted runs are also grouped into up to NBLOB separate
    objects per frame (one pass, no frame store): a run joins the blob
    whose box it touches (its columns within BLOB_CFG.GAP of the box's,
    its line at most GAP_Y + 1 below the box's last line: a car's roof
    and body, apart where its windows break the paint, are one object
    with GAP_Y as tall as the windows); a run touching
    several blobs joins them into one; a run touching none starts a new
    blob in a free slot. A blob no run has reached for GAP_Y + 1 lines is
    closed; a closed blob of fewer than BLOB_CFG.KEEP pixels is dropped
    (its slot reused), so small clutter does not use up the slots. With
    every slot taken, a new run is not grouped (BLOB_LOST counts it).
    With TERM_B, term A's runs use slots 0 .. NBLOB/2 - 1 and term B's
    the others, so a painted bus never joins the edges of the buildings
    behind it. At the end of the frame BLOB_X / BLOB_Y / BLOB_N[i] hold
    blob i (BLOB_N = 0: no blob, or one of fewer than KEEP pixels).
  - At the end of the frame (the tlast of line FRAME_SIZE height - 1)
    COUNT, BOX_X, BOX_Y and the sums are latched, FRAMES increments and
    done_o pulses for one clock. COUNT = 0: nothing found (the box then
    reads x0 > x1).
  - SCRATCH[0..27]: plain read / write words for the CPU (the tracking
    state of this detector: the firmware keeps one set per tracked
    object of the class).
Registers on the cfg_* / sts_* ports; object_tracker_top.sv is the
block with its AXI4-Lite register map (src/include/object_tracker_regs.sv): ID "OTRK" / VERSION / DATE at 0x00-0x08, CTRL 0x18,
FRAME_SIZE 0x1C, THRESH 0x20, WIN_X 0x24, WIN_Y 0x28, FRAMES 0x2C, COUNT
0x30, BOX_X 0x34, BOX_Y 0x38, SUM_X 0x3C, SUM_Y 0x40, STATUS 0x44, RUN
0x48, Y_RANGE 0x4C, CB_RANGE 0x50, CR_RANGE 0x54, SAT_MIN 0x58, BLOB_CFG
0x5C, SCRATCH 0x60 + 4 i (28 words), RUN_B 0xD0, BLOB_X 0x100 + 4 i,
BLOB_Y 0x120 + 4 i, BLOB_N 0x140 + 4 i (i < NBLOB = 8); ADDR_W = 9.
Clock - clk (pixel clock). Reset - synchronous active low rst_n.
Latency - results one clock after the last pixel of the frame.

object_tracker with its AXI4-Lite register interface, the
block designs and testbenches instantiate: the register map
object_tracker_regs (u_regs, src/include/object_tracker_regs.sv, ID
"OTRK", VERSION and DATE at 0x00-0x08, the registers from 0x10) and the
logic object_tracker (u_core, src/object_tracker.sv), joined by their
register ports (cfg_* to the logic, sts_* back). Generated by
ip/scripts/regmap_gen.py from object_tracker_regs.json and the ports of
object_tracker: regenerate after changing either. Clock - clk. Reset -
synchronous active low rst_n.
```

Describe and handle the edge cases, error recovery, latency and configuration-change rules stated above; where the text is silent, choose the safe option and document it in the file header.

## 6a. Industry reference check

Comparison of section 6 with published engineering references. Every difference is a `TODO(REF-...)` written as a prompt for updating the design.

```text
// Industry reference check - object_tracker (2026-10-16)
// Sources:
//   [1] D. G. Bailey, C. T. Johnston, "Single pass connected components analysis", IVCNZ 2007;
//   N. Ma, D. G. Bailey, C. T. Johnston, "Optimised single pass connected components analysis",
//   FPT 2008, https://sfat.massey.ac.nz/research/centres/crisp/pdfs/2008_FPT_185.pdf; MathWorks
//   Vision HDL blob analysis https://www.mathworks.com/help/visionhdl/ug/blob-analysis.html
//   [2] ITU-R BT.601-7 (2011) https://www.itu.int/rec/R-REC-BT.601 and BT.709-6 (2015)
//   https://www.itu.int/rec/R-REC-BT.709 - Kr/Kb 0.299/0.114 and 0.2126/0.0722, 8-bit Y = 16 +
//   219 E'Y, C = 128 + 224 E'C; scaled equations in Linux V4L2 colorspaces
//   https://docs.kernel.org/7.1/_sources/userspace-api/media/v4l/colorspaces-details.rst.txt
// Published algorithm / equations:
//   Streaming blob analysis: single-pass connected-components labelling of runs, merging labels
//   when a run touches several, per-blob bounding box / area / centroid sums, no frame store
//   (Bailey & Johnston). Colour tests in YCbCr per BT.601: Cb = 128 + 0.564 (B - Y), Cr = 128 +
//   0.713 (R - Y).
// Comparison with this IP (section 6):
//   Matches: run-length based single-pass grouping with merges, boxes, counts and sums, slot
//   reuse. Differs: grouping uses box proximity (GAP / GAP_Y) rather than strict 8-connectivity
//   (intentional, joins parts split by windows); luma (R + 2G + B) / 4 and chroma (B - Y) / 2,
//   (R - Y) / 2 approximate BT.601 (0.564 and 0.713 scale factors), so skin-tone / colour
//   ranges tuned on standard YCbCr do not carry over directly.
// TODO(REF-OBJECT_TRACKER-1) [LOW] Colour space approximation. Prompt: in
//   ip/video/object_tracker/src/object_tracker.sv header, state that Y / Cb / Cr are the
//   approximations Y = (R + 2G + B) / 4, Cb = 128 + (B - Y) / 2, Cr = 128 + (R - Y) / 2 (not
//   BT.601) and how to convert BT.601 ranges to them, or switch to the BT.601 integer matrix of
//   isp_csc (shared function) and update the testbench model; also document that grouping uses
//   box proximity, not pixel connectivity.
```

### Register map (from `object_tracker_regs.json`)

| Offset | Name | Access | Reset | Description | Fields |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0x00 | ID | RO | "OTRK" | IP identifier, 4 ASCII characters (first in [31:24]) | - |
| 0x04 | VERSION | RO | - | version, ASCII "d.dd" (+0.01 at every source update) | - |
| 0x08 | DATE | RO | - | date of the last source update, BCD mm/dd/yyyy | - |
| 0x18 | CTRL | RW | 0 | control | EN[0] enable; POL[1] luma mode, 1: object darker than THRESH; MODE[2] 0 luma threshold, 1 colour ranges (Y_RANGE, CB_RANGE, CR_RANGE, SAT_MIN); MIN_RUN[11:8] shortest run counted when RUN.MIN_W = 0 (0 or 1: every pixel counts); FEAT_A[13:12] term A: 0 the luma / colour test, 1 it or the motion feature, 2 it and the motion feature, 3 the motion feature; TERM_B[14] term B on: the edge feature, in runs of RUN_B (its own blob slots) |
| 0x1C | FRAME_SIZE | RW | 0 | frame size | WIDTH[15:0] width; HEIGHT[31:16] height |
| 0x20 | THRESH | RW | 0 | luma threshold | - |
| 0x24 | WIN_X | RW | 0 | search window columns (inclusive, taken at the frame start) | X0[15:0] first; X1[31:16] last |
| 0x28 | WIN_Y | RW | 0 | search window lines | Y0[15:0] first; Y1[31:16] last |
| 0x2C | FRAMES | RO | 0 | frames measured | - |
| 0x30 | COUNT | RO | 0 | object pixels in the last frame (0: nothing found) | - |
| 0x34 | BOX_X | RO | 0 | object box columns of the last frame | X_MIN[15:0] min; X_MAX[31:16] max |
| 0x38 | BOX_Y | RO | 0 | object box lines | Y_MIN[15:0] min; Y_MAX[31:16] max |
| 0x3C | SUM_X | RO | 0 | sum of the object pixels' x (centroid = SUM_X / COUNT) | - |
| 0x40 | SUM_Y | RO | 0 | sum of their y | - |
| 0x44 | STATUS | RO | 0 | state | IN_FRAME[0] in a frame; FULL_WIN[1] the window of the frame being measured is the whole frame; BLOB_LOST[15:8] runs of the last frame not grouped into a blob (every slot taken; saturates at 255); FRAMES[31:16] FRAMES[15:0] |
| 0x48 | RUN | RW | 0 | run widths counted (a horizontal run of object pixels is judged when it ends) | MIN_W[11:0] shortest run (0: CTRL.MIN_RUN); MAX_W[27:16] longest run (0: no limit) |
| 0x4C | Y_RANGE | RW | 0xFF00 | colour mode: luma Y = (R + 2G + B) / 4 range | MIN[7:0] lowest; MAX[15:8] highest |
| 0x50 | CB_RANGE | RW | 0xFF00 | colour mode: Cb = 128 + (B - Y) / 2 range | MIN[7:0] lowest; MAX[15:8] highest |
| 0x54 | CR_RANGE | RW | 0xFF00 | colour mode: Cr = 128 + (R - Y) / 2 range | MIN[7:0] lowest; MAX[15:8] highest |
| 0x58 | SAT_MIN | RW | 0 | colour mode: lowest saturation \|Cb - 128\| + \|Cr - 128\| | - |
| 0x5C | BLOB_CFG | RW | 0x00000202 | blob grouping of the counted runs | GAP[7:0] a run joins a blob within GAP columns of its box; GAP_Y[15:8] and at most GAP_Y + 1 lines below its last line; KEEP[31:16] fewest pixels of a blob kept (a closed smaller blob frees its slot; reported only from KEEP pixels) |
| 0x60 + 4 i (i < 28) | SCRATCH | RW | 0 | CPU scratch words (the firmware's tracking state of this detector's objects) | - |
| 0xD0 | RUN_B | RW | 0 | term B run widths counted (judged when a run ends, by its whole length) | MIN_W[11:0] shortest run (0: 1); MAX_W[27:16] longest run (0: no limit) |
| 0x100 + 4 i (i < 8) | BLOB_X | RO | 0 | blob i columns at the end of the last frame (BLOB_N = 0: none) | X_MIN[15:0] min; X_MAX[31:16] max |
| 0x120 + 4 i (i < 8) | BLOB_Y | RO | 0 | blob i lines | Y_MIN[15:0] min; Y_MAX[31:16] max |
| 0x140 + 4 i (i < 8) | BLOB_N | RO | 0 | blob i pixels (0: no blob) | - |

## 7. Implementation constraints

- Synthesizable SystemVerilog-2012, technology independent (no vendor primitives; infer RAM and DSP).
- Must work in iverilog 12+ (`-g2012`), Verilator lint (`-Wall`, no UNOPTFLAT or latches) and Yosys.
- iverilog limits: declare before use; no enum ternaries without casts; no `break`; no arrays of queues; no `wait` on function calls; no declarations inside nested loop bodies of static initial blocks.
- No combinational path from a ready input back to a ready output; hoist scratch variables (no latches); split control and data `always_ff` blocks.
- One statement per line (`a <= b; c <= d;` is two lines; `if (x) y <= 1; else y <= 0;` is four).
- Instantiations: one parameter per line in `#( ... )` and one port per line, closing with `) u_name (` and `);` at the instance's indentation; a port-group macro is one port on its own line.
- Check with `python3 ip/scripts/sv_format.py --check <files>` (it can also rewrite: whitespace only, token-checked).
- Resources: Last Yosys synth_xilinx (7-series) result: about 1196 LUTs, 1046 flip-flops, 2 DSP48E1. Stay within about this budget.

## 9. Guidelines

Follow the design guidelines in `ip/docs/DESIGN_GUIDELINES.md` (complete rules; this prompt wins where it sets a value explicitly). In short:

- Synthesizable, technology-independent SystemVerilog-2012; behavioural models behind `` `ifdef SYNTHESIS `` black boxes; iverilog / Verilator / Yosys clean.
- Layout: one statement per line; one parameter and one port per line in instantiations; two-space indent; a comment on every port.
- Naming: `lower_snake_case` modules and files, `u_` instances, `g_` generate blocks, `UPPER_CASE` parameters, `_i` / `_o` / `_n` / `_t` port suffixes, `s_axis_` / `m_axis_` / `s_axil_` buses.
- Clocks and resets per domain, every crossing through a CDC technique (see the clocks section).
- AXI4-Stream data with back-pressure, AXI4-Lite control (ID / INFO registers, SLVERR out of range), defined switch-over points for configuration changes.
- Self-checking testbench with an independent model, named `test_<what>` tasks in `tb/tests/<name>_tests.sv`, gaps and back-pressure, a mutation check, 100 % code coverage.
- Diagrams: module and instance names, arrows from output to input, no crossing lines, every clock and reset domain labelled.

Guidelines file: `ip/docs/DESIGN_GUIDELINES.md`   (replace with your own guidelines file if needed)

## 12. Verification requirements

The reference testbench checks the following; the new testbench must cover at least the same:

```text
Self-checking testbench for object_tracker. axis_frame_bfm
sends test images on the observed stream; the stream's tready, which
object_tracker only watches, is driven by the testbench (random stalls
where a test asks for them). After every frame the results (COUNT,
BOX_X, BOX_Y, SUM_X, SUM_Y, FRAMES) are compared with track_ref's
measurement model for the window and settings the testbench expects
for that frame (window taken at the frame start). Tests: registers,
dark and bright objects, search window (also changed in the middle of
a frame), the run filter, an empty frame, disable, STATUS, random
images and settings with stalls, the colour mode (skin tone, saturated
paint, SAT_MIN), the run-width band (RUN.MIN_W / MAX_W), the scratch
words, random colour scenes, blobs, and the two terms: feat_i is the
pixel's own LSBs (edge = B[0], motion = G[0]) so the model sees the same
features (CTRL.FEAT_A, CTRL.TERM_B, RUN_B). Prints TEST PASSED on success; +vcd
dumps object_tracker_tb.vcd. The test tasks are in
tests/object_tracker_tests.sv (`included).
```

Also: an independent reference model (not a copy of the RTL); random input gaps and output back-pressure on every stream; register readback; edge cases; a mutation check (break one rule, show the testbench fails).

Every simulation script names the tests it can run: `ip/scripts/run_sim.sh object_tracker --list-tests` prints them (and every run prints them at its start). Put each test in its own `test_<what>` task in `tb/tests/<name>_tests.sv`, listed with a one-line description in that file's header.

Tests of the reference design (the new design must provide at least these):

| Testbench | Test | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `object_tracker_tb` | `test_registers` | control registers read back, reset results (COUNT 0, empty box) |
| `object_tracker_tb` | `test_dark_object` | A dark rectangle on a light scene: exact box, count and sums (whole-frame window) |
| `object_tracker_tb` | `test_bright_object` | CTRL.POL = 0: a bright object on a dark scene |
| `object_tracker_tb` | `test_window` | Window smaller than the object (box clipped to it); a window written in the middle of a frame applies from the next frame |
| `object_tracker_tb` | `test_run_filter` | Single-pixel specks and a 1-pixel-wide line are ignored with MIN_RUN 2 and counted with MIN_RUN 0 / 1; MIN_RUN 15 with runs of 14, 15 and 16 pixels |
| `object_tracker_tb` | `test_empty` | No object: COUNT 0, box x min > x max |
| `object_tracker_tb` | `test_disable` | CTRL.ENABLE = 0: no frame measured, no done_o |
| `object_tracker_tb` | `test_status` | STATUS[0] during a frame, STATUS[1] for a whole-frame window, STATUS[31:16] = FRAMES |
| `object_tracker_tb` | `test_random` | 24 random scenes, thresholds, polarities, run lengths and windows with random stalls |
| `object_tracker_tb` | `test_id_block` | ID "OTRK", VERSION ("d.dd") and DATE (BCD mm/dd/yyyy) at the base address, read only (SLVERR); the rest of the map from 0x10 |
| `object_tracker_tb` | `test_colour` | CTRL.MODE = 1: a skin-tone patch (face) and a saturated red patch (car paint) on a grey scene; each colour range picks only its own patch, SAT_MIN rejects the grey; reset ranges read back |
| `object_tracker_tb` | `test_run_band` | RUN.MIN_W / MAX_W: of runs 6, 12 and 30 pixels wide, a band keeps only those inside it (a run is judged when it ends, at a non-object pixel or the end of the line, by its whole length: a run longer than MAX_W reaching into the window is not counted) |
| `object_tracker_tb` | `test_scratch` | SCRATCH[0..27] read back what was written, each its own word |
| `object_tracker_tb` | `test_blobs` | Three dark objects, specks and a U shape: one blob each, small ones dropped (KEEP), the U joined into one, GAP, GAP_Y; more objects than slots (BLOB_LOST); random scenes and BLOB_CFG against the model |
| `object_tracker_tb` | `test_random_colour` | 16 random colour scenes and settings with stalls |
| `object_tracker_tb` | `test_terms` | Two terms (feat_i = the pixel's LSBs): CTRL.FEAT_A 0-3 (test, test or motion, test and motion, motion), CTRL.TERM_B with RUN_B (edges, own blob slots), RUN_B read back, random features and settings with stalls |

Code coverage (`make cov`, `ip/scripts/run_cov.sh`): every target is 100 % by default. A target may be lowered only here, per metric, with the reason; every item left uncovered is listed with its justification (unreachable by design, tied-off parameter, ...).

| Metric | Target |
|--------|--------|
| Line (statement) | 100 % |
| Branch (if / case arms, ternaries) | 100 % |
| Expression / condition | 100 % |
| Toggle (every bit 0->1 and 1->0) | 100 % |
| FSM state and transition | 100 % |
| Functional (a cover point / cover property per requirement, mode and corner) | 100 % |
| Assertions (every SVA property exercised, none failing) | 100 % |

Pass criteria: `make -C video/object_tracker test` passes, every coverage target met, Verilator lint clean, `sv_format.py --check` clean, `make synth` passes.

## 13. Report back

Files created, register map, the test list with results (with the mutation check), coverage per metric (and every waiver), synthesis resources, any change to existing IP and why, known limits.
